description: Original independent C2 Plastic Ocean review-based test proposal pending human audit.

tabs.title: Narratives and Responsibility
tabs.description: Critically assess the documentarian's construction of causation.

tabs.title: Public Reasoning
tabs.description: Apply the author's critique to environmental claims.

questions.q: What makes the screening's overflowing bin more significant than a simple accusation of hypocrisy?
choices: It proves that the teenager did not really use a flask for three years.
It demonstrates that screenings can never reduce disposable waste.
It makes the documentary's personal example completely false.
It exposes institutional conditions left outside the film's model of responsibility.
questions.explanation: The opening juxtaposes a visible personal hero with the unseen venue arrangements.

questions.q: How does the 'perfect consumer' narrative influence viewers' understanding of causation?
choices: It provides a complete account of the municipal waste system.
It favours easily filmed individual acts over less visible procurement and infrastructure.
It demonstrates that individual decisions have no consequences.
It gives equal narrative weight to institutions and people.
questions.explanation: The text argues that omitted systemic details reflect a choice about causation.

questions.q: Why does the author describe the family's recycling sequence as narratively convenient?
choices: It offers a legible, uplifting action while ignoring what happens further along the system.
It shows that the family refuses to cooperate with waste collection.
It establishes that sorting waste is the only environmental action.
It questions whether the family actually lives in the town.
questions.explanation: The municipal plant's absence illustrates the limitations of the neatly resolved montage.

questions.q: What is the function of the author's refusal to dismiss the organisers merely as hypocrites?
choices: It absolves every organisation of responsibility for waste.
It implies that venues should never attempt reusable systems.
It separates a valid logistical constraint from the film's misleading moral framing.
It reduces environmental responsibility solely to personal choice.
questions.explanation: Paragraph two acknowledges practical barriers while maintaining the need to analyse arrangements.

questions.q: What is the significance of describing systemic determinism as an 'equally flattering absolution'?
choices: Consumers have no influence on public facilities.
Institutional measures should always precede individual changes.
The teenager's flask proves that collective policy is unnecessary.
Blaming only institutions can excuse personal agency just as individual moralism excuses institutions.
questions.explanation: The author rejects both extremes and describes how everyday habits and public provision interact.

questions.q: Why is the metal flask example framed as context-dependent rather than inherently virtuous?
choices: Every reusable item is more harmful than a disposable cup.
Production, lifespan and actual use determine its comparative effects.
The teenager could not have influenced other students.
The film must calculate a universal environmental score.
questions.explanation: Paragraph five contrasts the symbol with the conditions needed to judge its impact.

questions.q: What would be a more intellectually demanding edit of the festival deposit-cup trial?
choices: Present only the successful shots to encourage immediate action.
Interpret a poor first year as proof that reuse never works.
Show both reduced litter and missing returns, then examine how costs were measured.
Avoid mention of the staff or people responsible for collecting cups.
questions.explanation: The author argues that the same evidence can be edited into either triumph or failure.

questions.q: How does the writer qualify the claim that urgency justifies simplifying environmental films?
choices: Emotion can motivate action, but urgency does not excuse inaccuracies or unexamined uncertainty.
Any urgency necessarily makes a film less persuasive.
Viewers can only act after reading a complete technical report.
Artistic clarity is impossible without removing all emotion.
questions.explanation: Paragraph six concedes the importance of an engaging film but insists on precision.

questions.q: Why would an ending that offers questions rather than moral innocence be preferable?
choices: It allows the audience to leave without considering responsibility.
It equips viewers to identify missing actors and test an appealing explanation.
It ensures that no individual changes their habits.
It gives the filmmaker a more dramatic closing soundtrack.
questions.explanation: The conclusion values a framework for critical inquiry over temporary virtue.

questions.q: What is the strongest objection to treating either private habits or public infrastructure as entirely sufficient?
choices: A single private act must always lead to a new public policy.
Public institutions cannot respond to choices made by consumers.
Environmental outcomes are independent of the systems available.
They influence each other through demand, collective action, provision and practice.
questions.explanation: The text explicitly describes traffic between private habit and public provision.
